label: the wrench (models/v_crowbar.mdl, models/p_crowbar.mdl, models/w_crowbar.mdl): a pipe wrench: red-painted handle worn to bare iron, a heavy toothed jaw

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_crowbar.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked C, A, C, A where the asset was D, B, D, A: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline reads as a hammer or sledge: a solid box head on a straight bar (sides.png, left and right views; lineup.png D). The brief asks for a pipe wrench, and the head has no opening, hinged jaw profile. Length and overall proportion are close to the brief's 18, so the fault is the head's form, not the size.

M2.reason: Measured size is 18.5 x 6 x 9.7. Length is 2.9% over the brief's 18, inside the 15% band.

M3.reason: The red handle with silver wear at its ends and the heavy jaw are there. The toothed jaw is weak: the teeth show only as a fine hatched strip on the head's underside (sides.png, top and below views) and two silver ribs on its face (front view), which do not read as teeth at game size. The head is a solid block with no opening jaw and no visible adjusting parts (the top view's two small squares are unclear), so the pipe wrench's form is missing.

M4.reason: The handle is red paint, and its ends and patches show bare silver (sides.png left view; in-hand.png). The head is dark grey-brown with silver bars. This matches the brief's red handle worn to iron, with no region off its colour.

M5.reason: The wear is a few small silver patches on the handle and its end caps (sides.png left and right views). The brief says the handle is worn to bare iron along its grip, and the handle is still mostly smooth red. The head's panel and rust detail is faint.

M6.reason: Line-up test on lineup.png: the judges picked C, A, C, A where the asset was D, B, D, A. The asset was caught once, in the last round, under the rule that a catch twice or more caps M6 at 1. So M6 passes at its cap of 2.

M7.reason: No origin or upright stance can be checked against the brief. The sides show the tool lying roughly flat with the handle going diagonally off the head (sides.png, lineup.png). Nothing in the pictures confirms it rests on its origin as a world weapon should.

M8.reason: SMAK's checks report no errors. It has 172 triangles, under the 187 that three quarters of Half-Life's props of its kind stay under and far under the 291 most spend. No face is open or inverted in the sides or in-hand views.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the mod's head sits low and centre, with its jaw at the bottom edge. Its handle is out of the frame. The game's crowbar sits high at the top right, so the wrench is not where the original sits. The handle and the hand are not visible in the still, so holding and the way round can't be confirmed. The attack frames (attack.png) show no part leaving the hands in the frames shown.
